scope: Selected England 2013 Science, Computing and Design & Technology programmes; NGSS 5-PS1-3 boundary only. Not an audit of all catalogued curricula.

statusDefinitions.Partial: A component is related to the named requirement; remaining conditions prevent a whole-expectation coverage claim.
statusDefinitions.Unverified: An exact standards association has not been established; absence of a link is not proof of universal curriculum absence.
statusDefinitions.Out of scope: The named assessment explicitly excludes this concept; scope is that expectation only.

records.contribution: The proposed density comparison is outside this particular performance expectation's assessment boundary.
records.remainingConditions: Do not map density mastery to 5-PS1-3. This is not a claim that all elementary curricula exclude density.

records.scope: England Science KS1–2 and KS3 Pressure in fluids
records.contribution: Displacement is a useful conceptual prerequisite/application for buoyancy; no exact primary expectation was established in this review.
records.remainingConditions: Do not infer full coverage of fluid pressure from displaced-volume comparisons; other jurisdictions remain unreviewed.

records.scope: England Science KS3 Pressure in fluids
records.contribution: Related to the later-stage floating/upthrust requirement; the primary-age claim supplies a bounded qualitative model.
records.remainingConditions: Does not cover the complete pressure strand, atmosphere or numerical pressure; proposed ages are not statutory age mappings.

records.scope: England Science KS3 Pressure in fluids
records.contribution: Direct conceptual overlap with depth-dependent liquid pressure; the proposed younger scope omits numerical requirements.
records.remainingConditions: The complete strand also includes atmospheric and force/area pressure. No primary statutory association is authored.

records.scope: England Computing KS2 and D&T KS2 technical knowledge
records.contribution: Explaining sensing/control/actuation supports physical-system programming and product control.
records.remainingConditions: The conceptual explanation alone does not demonstrate writing/debugging a program, decomposition or designing/making a product; see the D&T source as well.

records.scope: England Computing KS2 and D&T KS2 technical knowledge
records.contribution: Repeated measurement and correction can support programming, monitoring and control.
records.remainingConditions: This regulator model is an authored application, not an explicit primary requirement for closed-loop theory; explanation alone does not establish programming or making competence.

records.scope: England Science Year 5 Forces; D&T KS2 mechanical systems
records.contribution: Related primary content covers mechanisms that change force; the explicit input-travel and energy relationship adds depth.
records.remainingConditions: No numerical work or efficiency coverage; a concept task alone does not meet practical product-use conditions. Related examples do not certify every mechanism expectation.

records.scope: England D&T KS1 stability; Science KS3 turning effects
records.contribution: Qualitative stability prediction contributes to understanding structures; the explicit centre/support model extends the primary practical requirement.
records.remainingConditions: Does not cover actually building stronger/stiffer/stable structures; formal turning-effects content is later-stage. No KS1 age mapping is inferred for this 8–12 proposal.

records.scope: England Science KS3 pressure as force per area
records.contribution: The direction-of-change comparison addresses a qualitative component of later force/area pressure.
records.remainingConditions: Does not assess the numerical ratio or the whole pressure strand; primary-age use is proposed enrichment.

records.scope: England Science KS1–2 and D&T KS2 electrical systems
records.contribution: Related light, electricity and design content provides foundations; no exact primary panel-orientation requirement was established.
records.remainingConditions: Do not label a working circuit or generic energy-conversion standard fully covered by this orientation concept. Other jurisdictions were not checked.
